concurrency.rule: If available Codex concurrency is lower than 32, every assignment is still created and queued. When a task finishes, the next queued task starts immediately.
startOrder: SRC01-SRC04 and every PF lane holding families start together — the conveyor and the builders are not sequential
VF lanes start on the first PF checkpoint, not on a completed assignment
FIX lanes start on the first FAIL_REPAIR_REQUIRED verdict
an empty PF lane starts the moment a source lane releases a family into it
concurrency.idleRule: A lane is idle only when no executable work exists for its kind. An empty PF lane at dispatch is idle because the source queue is empty for it, and the source lanes are the work that ends that.

assignments.preflightMustReturn: PACKET_BUILD_ENVIRONMENT_READY with every registered applicable check passing
rasterRule: **A missing Chromium is not a source blocker and it is not a legal blocker.** ENV-RAS01 established that a Codex container cannot resolve or fetch one -- the Playwright CDN answers HTTP 403 from inside it. That is an environment fact about the container, not a fact about the packet, and classifying it as BLOCKED_SOURCE would put a packet defect on a record that has none.

**And if your container DOES resolve a browser, that changes nothing about whose raster counts.** Two lanes have now reported building a page image locally, and they were right to discard it: a local render is not a receipt. Only the central gate below produces one, bound to the exact bytes the queue pinned and published as an artifact this factory can admit. Use a local render to measure something if it helps you, delete it, and still return `BUILT_RASTER_PENDING` with `visualDefects` untouched.
Finish every nonvisual obligation. Record the exact SHA-256 of the canonical and boundary PDFs you produced. Return the family `BUILT_RASTER_PENDING`.

Put that in `rasterState`. `status` is the row's own outcome and takes exactly `COMPLETED` or `STOPPED`: a repair that finished is `COMPLETED` even though nobody has rastered it, because `status` records whether YOU finished, not whether a page was looked at. The post-repair reader in `generate.mjs` takes only rows whose `status` is `COMPLETED`, so a finished repair filed as `BUILT_RASTER_PENDING` leaves its family sitting in FAIL.

`countersBefore` and `countersAfter` hold exactly the nine counters and nothing else -- that reader requires every value to be numerically zero, so a prose key alongside them (`measuredBy`, a caveat, even a boolean `allNineZero`) makes the whole object read as non-zero. Put the prose in siblings and keep every word of it.

`BUILT_RASTER_PENDING` is a factory workflow state and not a launch verdict. It zeroes nothing and waives nothing: visualDefects stays whatever it is, because it records that nobody has looked, not that there is nothing to see. **No packet becomes PASS_COMPLETE without RASTER_PASS.**

The render happens in `.github/workflows/rcap-packet-raster-acceptance-batch.yml` on a browser-equipped runner, against the exact bytes your hashes pin. RASTER_PASS sends the family to independent verification; RASTER_FAIL sends it to FIX.
Page rasters go through `scripts/raster/pdf-page-raster.mjs`. It discovers its own browser and calibrates the page-to-pixel mapping against both the paper bounds and stamped marks.
NEVER `pdftoppm`. NEVER `apt-get`. NEVER `playwright install`. The environment refuses package installation and a Poppler fallback is not a fallback, it is a different measurement.
The preflight now gates on the rasterizer resolving a browser it can execute, so a lane that cannot raster learns before it builds rather than after.
claimRule: Assert only these 2 exact families before reading or writing family content:
`node scripts/grade-a-packet-factory-24h/claim.mjs --assert PF01 'nc_145_8a_youthful-set'`
`node scripts/grade-a-packet-factory-24h/claim.mjs --assert PF01 'ar-act346-set'`
A non-zero exit is a full stop for that family: report `BLOCKED_BEFORE_CLAIM` naming the exact refusal, and read none of its artifacts.
Do not release a claim in a worker return. Captain releases it centrally after integrating the bounded return.
assignments.theDiffIsTheReturn: Commit locally. Leave the final diff for the Codex Cloud interface. There is no PUSHED line in a cloud return.
assignments.mission: Build 2 packet families to the builder contract, one at a time, checkpointing as you go. A family that stops does not stop the lane.

rowStopContract.everyFamilyGetsExactlyOneRow: COMPLETED or STOPPED, one row per assigned family, no family missing and none twice. A lane that returns fewer rows than it was assigned families has lost work silently.

rowStopContract.theLaneCompletesNormally: A lane with blocked families still completes. Blocked rows are the finding, not a failure of the lane.

**And if your container DOES resolve a browser, that changes nothing about whose raster counts.** Two lanes have now reported building a page image locally, and they were right to discard it: a local render is not a receipt. Only the central gate below produces one, bound to the exact bytes the queue pinned and published as an artifact this factory can admit. Put that in `rasterState`. `status` is the row's own outcome and takes exactly `COMPLETED` or `STOPPED`: a repair that finished is `COMPLETED` even though nobody has rastered it, because `status` records whether YOU finished, not whether a page was looked at. The post-repair reader in `generate.mjs` takes only rows whose `status` is `COMPLETED`, so a finished repair filed as `BUILT_RASTER_PENDING` leaves its family sitting in FAIL.

`countersBefore` and `countersAfter` hold exactly the nine counters and nothing else -- that reader requires every value to be numerically zero, so a prose key alongside them (`measuredBy`, a caveat, even a boolean `allNineZero`) makes the whole object read as non-zero. Put the prose in siblings and keep every word of it.

rasterRule: **A missing Chromium is not a source blocker and it is not a legal blocker.** ENV-RAS01 established that a Codex container cannot resolve or fetch one -- the Playwright CDN answers HTTP 403 from inside it. That is an environment fact about the container, not a fact about the packet, and classifying it as BLOCKED_SOURCE would put a packet defect on a record that has none.

**And if your container DOES resolve a browser, that changes nothing about whose raster counts.** Two lanes have now reported building a page image locally, and they were right to discard it: a local render is not a receipt. Only the central gate below produces one, bound to the exact bytes the queue pinned and published as an artifact this factory can admit. Use a local render to measure something if it helps you, delete it, and still return `BUILT_RASTER_PENDING` with `visualDefects` untouched.
Finish every nonvisual obligation. Record the exact SHA-256 of the canonical and boundary PDFs you produced. Return the family `BUILT_RASTER_PENDING`.

Put that in `rasterState`. `status` is the row's own outcome and takes exactly `COMPLETED` or `STOPPED`: a repair that finished is `COMPLETED` even though nobody has rastered it, because `status` records whether YOU finished, not whether a page was looked at. The post-repair reader in `generate.mjs` takes only rows whose `status` is `COMPLETED`, so a finished repair filed as `BUILT_RASTER_PENDING` leaves its family sitting in FAIL.

`countersBefore` and `countersAfter` hold exactly the nine counters and nothing else -- that reader requires every value to be numerically zero, so a prose key alongside them (`measuredBy`, a caveat, even a boolean `allNineZero`) makes the whole object read as non-zero. Put the prose in siblings and keep every word of it.

`BUILT_RASTER_PENDING` is a factory workflow state and not a launch verdict. It zeroes nothing and waives nothing: visualDefects stays whatever it is, because it records that nobody has looked, not that there is nothing to see. **No packet becomes PASS_COMPLETE without RASTER_PASS.**

The render happens in `.github/workflows/rcap-packet-raster-acceptance-batch.yml` on a browser-equipped runner, against the exact bytes your hashes pin. RASTER_PASS sends the family to independent verification; RASTER_FAIL sends it to FIX.
Page rasters go through `scripts/raster/pdf-page-raster.mjs`. It discovers its own browser and calibrates the page-to-pixel mapping against both the paper bounds and stamped marks.
NEVER `pdftoppm`. NEVER `apt-get`. NEVER `playwright install`. The environment refuses package installation and a Poppler fallback is not a fallback, it is a different measurement.
The preflight now gates on the rasterizer resolving a browser it can execute, so a lane that cannot raster learns before it builds rather than after.

REPEATING ROWS: no row carries written cells beside required cells left blank
PROTECTED FIELDS: no signature, signature date, certificate of mailing, court-only or prosecutor-only field carries ink
ARTIFACTS: canonical and boundary bytes hash to what the record names
PAGE ORDER: the rendered page order matches the packet manifest
CLIPPING AND OVERLAP: no ink outside a measured write box
FILING DESTINATION: the instructions name the court or agency the route names

The committed assignment contains exactly 0 itemIds; iterate those values only. A familyId is metadata and is not a source claim key.
A non-zero exit stops that row only: record `BLOCKED_BEFORE_CLAIM`, read none of its evidence, and continue with unrelated obligations.
Release each completed obligation independently: `node scripts/grade-a-packet-factory-24h/claim.mjs --release DISC01 <itemId>`.
assignments.theDiffIsTheReturn: Commit locally. Leave the final diff for the Codex Cloud interface. There is no PUSHED line in a cloud return.
assignments.mission: Turn a descriptive label into a document identity: exact form number, official publisher, revision and the official URL it is published at. Resolve against committed inventories; never guess a form number. No obligation of this class is queued for this host group at dispatch; the lane starts the moment one arrives.

sourceRelationshipRegistry.readItBeforeYouFetchAnything: Look your obligation up by jurisdiction and canonical artifact id. Its sourceState tells you whether there is anything to fetch at all.

statesThatAreNotAFetch.BUNDLE_COMPONENT: 0 — the document is a page inside a public bundle whose address is already recorded. Record the component locator and alias. Acquire the BUNDLE once, never the page.
statesThatAreNotAFetch.EMBEDDED_SECTION: 0 — the document is a section inside another form. There is no separate binary to request from anyone.
statesThatAreNotAFetch.STALE_OR_VARIANT_ID: 0 — the identity is missing its current suffix or its filing-mode variant. Normalize the identity first; the form is public.
statesThatAreNotAFetch.SOURCE_SCOPE_AND_VERSION_AMBIGUITY: 0 — statewide versus local scope is unsettled. Settle the scope before any inquiry.
statesThatAreNotAFetch.FAMILY_IDENTITY_AMBIGUOUS: 1 — several held artifacts match this identity. Which one the route requires is the question; do not pick one.
statesThatAreNotAFetch.CURRENTNESS_UNVERIFIED: 7 — the corpus already HOLDS matching bytes. The open question is whether the publisher still issues that edition. This is not a missing source and it is not an acquisition.
statesThatAreNotAFetch.STATUTORY_CUSTOM_PLEADING: 0 — a statutory citation. There is no document at the other end; a packet-build lane drafts against the statute.
statesThatAreNotAFetch.LICENSE_PERMISSION_REVIEW: 0 — the form is public and its publisher restricts commercial reuse. Counsel and business decide, not a clerk.

statesThatAreAFetch.MISSING_SOURCE_BINARY: 0 — expected and absent; acquire once an exact address is settled.
statesThatAreAFetch.MISSING_CANONICAL_RELATIONSHIP_METADATA: 10 — no publisher, address or locator is recorded. Settle identity before fetching.

sourceRelationshipRegistry.neverAskAClerkWhenAPublicSourceIsKnown: The previous human queue told a person to contact a clerk 101 times. Zero of the top twenty justified it. If the registry records an official source page, the answer is already known.
sourceRelationshipRegistry.youDoNotDecideReuse: A publisher's commercial-reuse restriction is a counsel and business decision. Record it; do not resolve it and do not ask a clerk about it.

assignments.boundedBy: the issuing court or agency that publishes the document
assignments.leverageRule: Settle the documents at the top of this list first. Leverage is counted per DOCUMENT: acquiring one form releases every family waiting on it, and one form can gate ten families while the next gates one.
assignments.whatTheLastBatchTaught: On 2026-08-31 an acquisition batch fetched thirty documents successfully and unblocked zero families — all thirty belonged to jurisdictions already resolved, with no overlap against the 238 documents gating the 256 blocked families. Fetch capacity is not the constraint. Knowing which document to fetch is.
assignments.countMeaning: families this lane would release if all of its obligations resolve. It is not a count of promoted sources and must not be read as one.
assignments.familiesUnblockedIsProspectiveAlias: kept so an existing reader does not silently see zero; it means familiesThisLaneWouldRelease and nothing more
assignments.splitFamilyRule: A family whose obligations are split across lanes is released by no single lane. You advance it; the family is released when the last of the named lanes clears its share. Reporting it released alone is a duplicate release and is refused at integration.
assignments.handsOffTo: ACQ, the moment an exact official URL is known — do not wait for the rest of this lane
assignments.dispatchImmediately: The moment you know an exact official URL, hand it to the ACQ lane for this host. Do not hold it until the rest of your obligations resolve.
assignments.releaseRule: Prospective release is never actual release. Record familiesActuallyReleasedNow only after every remaining source binds; otherwise it is an empty array.
assignments.continueAfterFailure: An obligation that cannot be settled is a STOPPED row. The lane continues to the next one.
assignments.egressReality: This environment refuses outbound egress to court and agency hosts. Identity and inventory work runs here; anything needing a fetch is dispatched through the acquisition workflow, never attempted locally and never faked.
requiredOutputs: data/rcap-grade-a/packet-factory-24h/disc01/rows.json — one row per obligation: itemId, status, the identity or receipt, and the families it releases
data/rcap-grade-a/source-acquisition/packet-factory-24h/disc01/receipts.json — the eleven recorded fields per resolved source; no body is committed

outputSchema.rule: An unrecognised status is refused at integration rather than translated.

stopConditions: NEVER guess a form number and never accept an unofficial mirror. A secondary copy does not override an available official original.
NEVER commit a source body, an extracted archive or anything under private/. A receipt carrying an exact hash is the deliverable.
NEVER promote a source without exact bytes. A promotion is a release, and a released family goes to a builder that will try to open the file.
LANE STOP — you build no packet and you touch no overlay directory.
ROW STOP — an obligation that cannot be settled here is STOPPED naming the exact host and the next operation that owns it.
returnFormat: DIFF LEFT FOR THE CODEX UI: YES
assignments.grantsNothing: A bound source is a bound source. It builds nothing, proves nothing and approves nothing.

assignments.mission: Take an acquired or reconciled artifact, register its custody, promote it into the governed index, and release every family whose last source is now bound. A promotion without exact bytes is refused. No obligation of this class is queued for this host group at dispatch; the lane starts the moment one arrives.

sourceRelationshipRegistry.readItBeforeYouFetchAnything: Look your obligation up by jurisdiction and canonical artifact id. Its sourceState tells you whether there is anything to fetch at all.

statesThatAreNotAFetch.BUNDLE_COMPONENT: 0 — the document is a page inside a public bundle whose address is already recorded. Record the component locator and alias. Acquire the BUNDLE once, never the page.
statesThatAreNotAFetch.EMBEDDED_SECTION: 0 — the document is a section inside another form. There is no separate binary to request from anyone.
statesThatAreNotAFetch.STALE_OR_VARIANT_ID: 0 — the identity is missing its current suffix or its filing-mode variant. Normalize the identity first; the form is public.
statesThatAreNotAFetch.SOURCE_SCOPE_AND_VERSION_AMBIGUITY: 0 — statewide versus local scope is unsettled. Settle the scope before any inquiry.
statesThatAreNotAFetch.FAMILY_IDENTITY_AMBIGUOUS: 1 — several held artifacts match this identity. Which one the route requires is the question; do not pick one.
statesThatAreNotAFetch.CURRENTNESS_UNVERIFIED: 7 — the corpus already HOLDS matching bytes. The open question is whether the publisher still issues that edition. This is not a missing source and it is not an acquisition.
statesThatAreNotAFetch.STATUTORY_CUSTOM_PLEADING: 0 — a statutory citation. There is no document at the other end; a packet-build lane drafts against the statute.
statesThatAreNotAFetch.LICENSE_PERMISSION_REVIEW: 0 — the form is public and its publisher restricts commercial reuse. Counsel and business decide, not a clerk.

statesThatAreAFetch.MISSING_SOURCE_BINARY: 0 — expected and absent; acquire once an exact address is settled.
statesThatAreAFetch.MISSING_CANONICAL_RELATIONSHIP_METADATA: 10 — no publisher, address or locator is recorded. Settle identity before fetching.

sourceRelationshipRegistry.neverAskAClerkWhenAPublicSourceIsKnown: The previous human queue told a person to contact a clerk 101 times. Zero of the top twenty justified it. If the registry records an official source page, the answer is already known.
sourceRelationshipRegistry.youDoNotDecideReuse: A publisher's commercial-reuse restriction is a counsel and business decision. Record it; do not resolve it and do not ask a clerk about it.

assignments.boundedBy: the custody register and the governed corpus index
assignments.leverageRule: Settle the documents at the top of this list first. Leverage is counted per DOCUMENT: acquiring one form releases every family waiting on it, and one form can gate ten families while the next gates one.
assignments.whatTheLastBatchTaught: On 2026-08-31 an acquisition batch fetched thirty documents successfully and unblocked zero families — all thirty belonged to jurisdictions already resolved, with no overlap against the 238 documents gating the 256 blocked families. Fetch capacity is not the constraint. Knowing which document to fetch is.
assignments.countMeaning: families this lane would release if all of its obligations resolve. It is not a count of promoted sources and must not be read as one.
assignments.familiesUnblockedIsProspectiveAlias: kept so an existing reader does not silently see zero; it means familiesThisLaneWouldRelease and nothing more
assignments.splitFamilyRule: A family whose obligations are split across lanes is released by no single lane. You advance it; the family is released when the last of the named lanes clears its share. Reporting it released alone is a duplicate release and is refused at integration.
assignments.handsOffTo: Captain, who assigns every released family to the next available PF lane immediately
assignments.dispatchImmediately: The moment a family's last source is promoted, report it released. Captain assigns it to the next available PF lane without waiting for this lane to finish.
assignments.promotionRule: A source is promoted only with exact bytes: a custody path that exists and a SHA-256 that matches the indexed entry. A promotion without bytes releases a family into a builder that cannot open its source.
assignments.releaseRule: Prospective release is never actual release. Record familiesActuallyReleasedNow only after every remaining source binds; otherwise it is an empty array.
assignments.continueAfterFailure: An obligation that cannot be settled is a STOPPED row. The lane continues to the next one.
assignments.egressReality: This environment refuses outbound egress to court and agency hosts. Identity and inventory work runs here; anything needing a fetch is dispatched through the acquisition workflow, never attempted locally and never faked.

ROW STOP — an obligation that cannot be settled here is STOPPED naming the exact host and the next operation that owns it.

rasterRule: **A missing Chromium is not a source blocker and it is not a legal blocker.** ENV-RAS01 established that a Codex container cannot resolve or fetch one -- the Playwright CDN answers HTTP 403 from inside it. That is an environment fact about the container, not a fact about the packet, and classifying it as BLOCKED_SOURCE would put a packet defect on a record that has none.

**And if your container DOES resolve a browser, that changes nothing about whose raster counts.** Two lanes have now reported building a page image locally, and they were right to discard it: a local render is not a receipt. Only the central gate below produces one, bound to the exact bytes the queue pinned and published as an artifact this factory can admit. Use a local render to measure something if it helps you, delete it, and still return `BUILT_RASTER_PENDING` with `visualDefects` untouched.
Finish every nonvisual obligation. Record the exact SHA-256 of the canonical and boundary PDFs you produced. Return the family `BUILT_RASTER_PENDING`.

Put that in `rasterState`. `status` is the row's own outcome and takes exactly `COMPLETED` or `STOPPED`: a repair that finished is `COMPLETED` even though nobody has rastered it, because `status` records whether YOU finished, not whether a page was looked at. The post-repair reader in `generate.mjs` takes only rows whose `status` is `COMPLETED`, so a finished repair filed as `BUILT_RASTER_PENDING` leaves its family sitting in FAIL.

`countersBefore` and `countersAfter` hold exactly the nine counters and nothing else -- that reader requires every value to be numerically zero, so a prose key alongside them (`measuredBy`, a caveat, even a boolean `allNineZero`) makes the whole object read as non-zero. Put the prose in siblings and keep every word of it.

`BUILT_RASTER_PENDING` is a factory workflow state and not a launch verdict. It zeroes nothing and waives nothing: visualDefects stays whatever it is, because it records that nobody has looked, not that there is nothing to see. **No packet becomes PASS_COMPLETE without RASTER_PASS.**

The render happens in `.github/workflows/rcap-packet-raster-acceptance-batch.yml` on a browser-equipped runner, against the exact bytes your hashes pin. RASTER_PASS sends the family to independent verification; RASTER_FAIL sends it to FIX.
Page rasters go through `scripts/raster/pdf-page-raster.mjs`. It discovers its own browser and calibrates the page-to-pixel mapping against both the paper bounds and stamped marks.
NEVER `pdftoppm`. NEVER `apt-get`. NEVER `playwright install`. The environment refuses package installation and a Poppler fallback is not a fallback, it is a different measurement.
The preflight now gates on the rasterizer resolving a browser it can execute, so a lane that cannot raster learns before it builds rather than after.

rasterRule: **A missing Chromium is not a source blocker and it is not a legal blocker.** ENV-RAS01 established that a Codex container cannot resolve or fetch one -- the Playwright CDN answers HTTP 403 from inside it. That is an environment fact about the container, not a fact about the packet, and classifying it as BLOCKED_SOURCE would put a packet defect on a record that has none.

**And if your container DOES resolve a browser, that changes nothing about whose raster counts.** Two lanes have now reported building a page image locally, and they were right to discard it: a local render is not a receipt. Only the central gate below produces one, bound to the exact bytes the queue pinned and published as an artifact this factory can admit. Use a local render to measure something if it helps you, delete it, and still return `BUILT_RASTER_PENDING` with `visualDefects` untouched.
Finish every nonvisual obligation. Record the exact SHA-256 of the canonical and boundary PDFs you produced. Return the family `BUILT_RASTER_PENDING`.

Put that in `rasterState`. `status` is the row's own outcome and takes exactly `COMPLETED` or `STOPPED`: a repair that finished is `COMPLETED` even though nobody has rastered it, because `status` records whether YOU finished, not whether a page was looked at. The post-repair reader in `generate.mjs` takes only rows whose `status` is `COMPLETED`, so a finished repair filed as `BUILT_RASTER_PENDING` leaves its family sitting in FAIL.

`countersBefore` and `countersAfter` hold exactly the nine counters and nothing else -- that reader requires every value to be numerically zero, so a prose key alongside them (`measuredBy`, a caveat, even a boolean `allNineZero`) makes the whole object read as non-zero. Put the prose in siblings and keep every word of it.

**And if your container DOES resolve a browser, that changes nothing about whose raster counts.** Two lanes have now reported building a page image locally, and they were right to discard it: a local render is not a receipt. failedObligations.finding: This is the question this lane was asked to answer, and the answer is that the gap is real. The Colorado Judicial Department publishes JDF 491, 'Guide to Sealing Non-Conviction Records (simplified process)', at revision R: August 7, 2024 — the same revision date as both bound forms. Its step 2, headed 'File the Request — File these forms into your criminal case', names four forms with no branch and no condition between them: JDF 477 Motion, JDF 492 Order (just do §§ A-C), JDF 493 Notice (Just do §§ A-C), and JDF 478 Order (just do §§ A-C). Page 2 confirms it is one process, for cases ending in acquittal, a completed diversion agreement, a completed deferred judgment or a vacated conviction, under C.R.S. §§ 24-72-705 and 707 — the same statute and the same dispositions as this route. The packet delivers two of those four. rasterRule: **A missing Chromium is not a source blocker and it is not a legal blocker.** ENV-RAS01 established that a Codex container cannot resolve or fetch one -- the Playwright CDN answers HTTP 403 from inside it. That is an environment fact about the container, not a fact about the packet, and classifying it as BLOCKED_SOURCE would put a packet defect on a record that has none.

**And if your container DOES resolve a browser, that changes nothing about whose raster counts.** Two lanes have now reported building a page image locally, and they were right to discard it: a local render is not a receipt. Only the central gate below produces one, bound to the exact bytes the queue pinned and published as an artifact this factory can admit. Use a local render to measure something if it helps you, delete it, and still return `BUILT_RASTER_PENDING` with `visualDefects` untouched.
Finish every nonvisual obligation. Record the exact SHA-256 of the canonical and boundary PDFs you produced. Return the family `BUILT_RASTER_PENDING`.

Put that in `rasterState`. `status` is the row's own outcome and takes exactly `COMPLETED` or `STOPPED`: a repair that finished is `COMPLETED` even though nobody has rastered it, because `status` records whether YOU finished, not whether a page was looked at. The post-repair reader in `generate.mjs` takes only rows whose `status` is `COMPLETED`, so a finished repair filed as `BUILT_RASTER_PENDING` leaves its family sitting in FAIL.

`countersBefore` and `countersAfter` hold exactly the nine counters and nothing else -- that reader requires every value to be numerically zero, so a prose key alongside them (`measuredBy`, a caveat, even a boolean `allNineZero`) makes the whole object read as non-zero. Put the prose in siblings and keep every word of it.

`BUILT_RASTER_PENDING` is a factory workflow state and not a launch verdict. It zeroes nothing and waives nothing: visualDefects stays whatever it is, because it records that nobody has looked, not that there is nothing to see. **No packet becomes PASS_COMPLETE without RASTER_PASS.**

The render happens in `.github/workflows/rcap-packet-raster-acceptance-batch.yml` on a browser-equipped runner, against the exact bytes your hashes pin. RASTER_PASS sends the family to independent verification; RASTER_FAIL sends it to FIX.
Page rasters go through `scripts/raster/pdf-page-raster.mjs`. It discovers its own browser and calibrates the page-to-pixel mapping against both the paper bounds and stamped marks.
NEVER `pdftoppm`. NEVER `apt-get`. NEVER `playwright install`. The environment refuses package installation and a Poppler fallback is not a fallback, it is a different measurement.
The preflight now gates on the rasterizer resolving a browser it can execute, so a lane that cannot raster learns before it builds rather than after.

THE DISCLOSURE IS EXEMPLARY AND I RECORD IT IN FULL. participant-instructions.md opens 'What is in this packet, and what is not', its second heading is 'Read this first: these three forms are not the filing', and it says in terms 'The petition itself is not in this packet, and neither is the proposed order. If you file only these three sheets, you have not asked the court for anything', and then that neither of the other two routes' own filings is built here either. filing-instructions.md carries a section headed 'What this packet does NOT contain', and production-field-map.json lists all ten under componentsOfThisFamilysOwnRoutesThatNothingBuilds. That disclosure is why this is a queue scope decision - widen this family or open two more - rather than a build error, and the build lane says so itself. ONE MORE THING I MEASURED THAT BEARS ON THE SCOPE DECISION: three sibling Indiana families - in-conviction-felony-set, in-conviction-misd-set and in-conviction-d6-set - each deliver a COMPLETE ten-page packet whose pages 7-10 are these very same three documents, and they deliver them BLANK. So the fill this family maps is genuinely owed work that nothing else does; it is simply attached to routes whose filings nobody builds.

No signature, signature date or court-only field carries a VALUE - both signature rules on the Appearance, the signature rule on Form ACR, all three cause-number lines and the full Social Security number box are empty on the delivered pages, and I confirmed each. THE FAILURE IS THAT FOUR CERTIFICATE-OF-SERVICE CONTROLS CARRY INK THIS BUILD DREW.
